content: orafce provides a subset of Oracle built-in packages/functions (dbms_output, dbms_alert partial, plvdate, utl_* partial, NVL, etc.) for compatibility, not full parity. Known gaps: only implements a subset of dbms_sql; VARCHAR2/NVARCHAR2 don't enforce Oracle's 4000-byte limit; length() semantics differ for byte vs char semantics; some functions changed volatility (stable vs immutable) across versions causing functional-index breakage; goal is reducing migration work, not 1:1 Oracle emulation. Bulk-collect/array-iteration Oracle patterns are unnecessary/wasteful in PG and orafce emulation of them has CPU/memory overhead at scale.
